description: A and B make the IDENTICAL insertion (`x = x + 5;`). Correspondence runs base->A and base->B only - never A<->B, in our implementation or in the papers - so two independently inserted statements have no counterpart to be identified through. Both copies land in G_M, x becomes 11 rather than 6, and Type I fires. HPR as specified, but a FALSE SEMANTIC CONFLICT: git unifies identical additions and produces exactly the program both developers wrote (6 2). The corpus's one fixture where the textual tool does better. Found by fuzz.py, not by hand.
category: false semantic conflict - git merges it correctly
